source.title_on_document: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier: Field Experimental Evidence of the Effects of AI on Knowledge Worker Productivity and Quality

supplement.where: No separate online supplement is mentioned. Appendices A-E are in this PDF (PDF pp. 44-58). The preregistration (osf.io/ytaev) was embargoed, 'available from the authors upon request' (PDF p. 9, fn. 2).
supplement.holds: Appendix D (PDF p. 53) says the creativity ratings of each subject's idea list are presented 'in Table 1', but Appendix D has no table. The only Table 1 in the PDF is the main-text composite-quality table. The diversity result has no numeric table anywhere in this PDF, only density plots (Figure 6, PDF p. 36, repeated as Appendix D Figure 1, PDF p. 53).

paper_design_summary: 758 BCG consultants were split into two separate experiments. Within each experiment they were randomly assigned to no AI, GPT-4, or GPT-4 plus a prompt-engineering overview, after a baseline task done without AI. In the inside-the-frontier experiment (385 consultants), participants developed a new shoe product over 18 questions (ideation, analysis, writing, persuasion). Human graders and GPT-4 scored quality, and the 10+ shoe ideas from question 1 were compared across participants with Universal Sentence Encoder similarity. In the outside-the-frontier experiment (373 consultants), participants wrote a brand recommendation from data and interviews, scored for correctness and recommendation quality.

assignment.what_was_assigned: Access to a GPT-4 tool (GPT Only), GPT-4 plus a prompt-engineering overview (GPT + Overview), or no AI (control) for the experimental task. Assignment was stratified on gender, location, tenure, openness to innovation, and native English status. All participants first did an assessment task without AI.
assignment.quote: Following this, participants were randomly assigned to one of three conditions to assess the influence of AI on their tasks, with these conditions being consistent across both experiments.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 7), Section 2; stratification PDF p. 10 (printed p. 6)
assignment.prereg_locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 5), Section 2 and fn. 2 (osf.io/ytaev, embargoed)

participants.exclusions: 852 consultants responded to the enrollment survey and 758 (about 89 percent) completed the experiment (PDF p. 9, fn. 3). The paper does not say whether the 94 non-completers had already been assigned, so no count at randomization is given. 385 of the 758 were in this experiment. Per-arm counts are not reported. Tables 1-3 report 385 observations.
participants.who: BCG individual-contributor strategy consultants, about 7 percent of the firm's global individual-contributor cohort
participants.country: Multinational (BCG offices around the world); no country breakdown given
participants.quote: Approximately half of the participants (385 consultants) tackled a series of tasks where they were prompted to conceptualize and develop new product ideas
participants.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 6), Section 2; Table 1, PDF p. 38 (printed p. 34)

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-4 (as available at end of April 2023), default system prompt and temperature, via a company platform built on the OpenAI API
ai_tool.how_used: Free ChatGPT-like interaction during the 90-minute experimental task; all prompts and responses logged. Appendix C reports high 'retainment' (copying of GPT-4 text into answers), mode about 0.87.

task.description: Develop a new shoe for an underserved market or sport over 18 questions: generate at least 10 ideas, pick the best, describe a prototype, plan launch steps, name it, segment the market, write slogans, a 500-word memo, focus-group plan, competitor list, inspirational memo, press release, and an HBR-style article outline (Appendix A). Baseline assessment task: same structure for a new drink, without AI.
task.duration: Assessment task 30 minutes; experimental task 90 minutes, participants had to stay for the full time (PDF p. 11, printed p. 7)

outcomes.name: Composite Quality (human graders): mean of two graders' scores per question, averaged over the 18 questions
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Each answered question graded by two human graders, 'from BCG, or MBA students at a top program' (PDF p. 13, fn. 6); 1-10 scale. Composite covers creativity, analytical, writing, and persuasiveness questions, so it is overall task quality, not creativity alone. Robustness variants: Table 1 cols 2-3 add the assessment-task score, demographics, and (col 3) AI-familiarity controls.

outcomes.name: Between-subject semantic similarity of shoe ideas (question 1), Universal Sentence Encoder
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Each of a subject's ~10 ideas is encoded with Google's Universal Sentence Encoder (512-dimensional); inner products with all ideas of other subjects in the same condition are averaged, then averaged over the subject's ideas to give a subject-level 'between semantic similarity'. Higher similarity means less variation. Sign reversed relative to diversity.

contrasts.reported: Density plot with arm means as unlabeled dashed vertical lines; GPT Only mean similarity lies to the right of (higher than) Control. Text: 'there is a marked reduction in the variability of these ideas compared to those not using AI.' No numbers, SEs, or tests printed.

eligibility.reason: S1 randomly assigned individual consultants to GPT-4 access (two arms) or no AI on a product-ideation task (385 people analyzed; per-arm counts not given). Outcomes scored on output include a USE-embedding diversity measure of the question-1 shoe ideas, a creativity rating of the idea lists (Appendix D), and human-graded composite quality. Caveat for extraction: the diversity and idea-list creativity results have no printed numbers in this working paper (figure only or text only); the composite quality is task quality, not creativity alone.

one_line_finding: Among 385 BCG consultants, GPT-4 access raised human-graded composite quality on a product-innovation task by 1.556 (GPT Only, SE 0.080) and 1.746 (GPT + Overview, SE 0.074) points over a control mean of 4.099 (Table 1, PDF p. 38), while USE similarity of the shoe ideas across people rose (less diversity) in both AI arms, shown only in Figure 6 (PDF p. 36).
open_questions: Appendix D cites a 'Table 1' with creativity ratings of the idea lists that does not appear in this PDF. Does the Organization Science 2026 version print numbers for the idea-list creativity rating and for the diversity contrast (means, SEs, tests)?
Per-arm counts at assignment and after exclusions are not reported; were the 94 enrollees who did not complete (852 to 758) already randomized?
Is the diversity analysis kept in the published version? The retrieval note says this could not be checked.
Graders were BCG staff or MBA students; coding as expert_raters versus human_raters needs a decision.
notes: Working-paper version (Sept 2023) only; the version of record (Organization Science 2026) was not available. The markdown file is truncated at Table 1; all later tables, figures, and appendices were checked on the PDF. Outcomes not listed because they are not creativity or diversity outcomes: task completion share (Table 2: GPT + Overview 0.111*** (0.020), GPT Only 0.090*** (0.021), control mean 0.824), time to reach the last question (Table 3), outside-the-frontier timing (Table 5), retainment of GPT text (Appendix C, process measure), and the qualitative Centaur/Cyborg typology from 244 consultants (Appendix E). The two AI arms share one control group; under codebook rule 8.3 the GPT Only arm is closest to free chatbot use.
